pr_title: Improve project_panel diagnostic icon knockout colors
pr_comments:
This is how it looks like:

(Updated version)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a5506a5-1dd4-4c14-a2b1-cc80dba937f9


There is one thing that is missing. We do dynamic style adjustments for the drag_over color here:

https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/516f7b364213b2bbc1a658295df96443aa885ca0/crates/project_panel/src/project_panel.rs#L2693

I would really like to maintain a state for the `drag_over_entries` just like we did with the `hovered_entries`, but unfortunately there is no `on_drag_over` function that i can pass a listener to like we did with `on_hover`. 

I think we should add this function (either in this PR or separately) to the `div` and make sure that the drag over color matches as well.
I wonder if we can achieve the same result without explicitly tracking hover state of an entry.

> I wonder if we can achieve the same result without explicitly tracking hover state of an entry.

I was trying that initially but could not get it to work... (might be a me issue though) 

I initially didn't want to add an additional state but ended up liking it. I prefer being very explicit about the background and border color in a single place instead of adjusting the colors in many different places. It makes it much easier to understand where the colors come from.

Paired on this with @danilo-leal. Although I'm not a big fan of tracking the hovered entries solely for the purpose of the UI, we did not find a straight-forward way to achieve this without tracking the state explicitly.
Would be great if anyone can come up with an approach without tracking this state explicitly, but let's get this in for now!

issue_context.title: Error indicators in project panel should use different border for selected files
issue_context.body: ### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it In #18182 error indicators were added. For the selected file, the border used for the error icon is of an incorrect color ### Environment Zed: v0.162.0 (Zed Nightly 55cd99cdc4d22bf82c0a59d8fa76f4ab9b85370c) OS: macOS 15.1.0 Memory: 8 GiB Architecture: aarch64
comments: I can change that later today if this is not intentional?

> I can change that later today if this is not intentional?

I think it doesn't look good, but I'd prefer to hear @danilo-leal's opinion on it

You're referring to the white stroke around the x, right? If that's the case, this is a bit challenging at the moment because these different states in the project panel items (like hover or selection) use colors that leverage opacity, whereas the diagnostic icon uses a solid color. If we use exactly the same token as we use for the states, the knockout effect wouldn't quite work.

That original PR was merged because I think we're in a good spot with icon positioning, API to do the icon knockout effect, and, generally, the functionality. But there's still room to make this perfect, which includes possibly refining the color tokens we use for project panel items, ensuring the knockout thing always works well.

Does this make sense?

> If that's the case, this is a bit challenging at the moment because these different states in the project panel items (like hover or selection) use colors that leverage opacity, whereas the diagnostic icon uses a solid color. If we use exactly the same token as we use for the states, the knockout effect wouldn't quite work. It seems like, when the file isn't in focus, the white stroke blends in with the background. Can't we update the decoration color depending on the status of the entry?

We can yeah, but it's what I said—other states of the project panel item use transparent colors, which means the icon stroke wouldn't blend perfectly as they do in the resting/default state. The solution seems to be _not_ in the color used by the icon, but rather in the color token itself.

> We can yeah, but it's what I said—other states of the project panel item use transparent colors, which means the icon stroke wouldn't blend perfectly as they do in the resting/default state. The solution seems to be _not_ in the color used by the icon, but rather in the color token itself.

Yeah, makes sense

@danilo-leal I did not understand this completely so I might be missing something, but I played around a little and I think `item_colors.selected` needs to be `item_colors.marked_active` instead. https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/093c9cc87b052c4bdf2afc09a6d52e86eb9c7d3d/crates/project_panel/src/project_panel.rs#L2808-L2812 `selected` and `default` are the same color here: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/093c9cc87b052c4bdf2afc09a6d52e86eb9c7d3d/crates/project_panel/src/project_panel.rs#L254-L264 For hovering we could use `item_colors.hover` (the screenshot removed the mouse, but its the hovering state): Would this work or am I missing something?
I think this works pretty well. I'm going to create a PR for this tmr. I think we should fix this before https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/18182 makes it into the normal release.

Yeah, good call @nilskch. I opened up https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/20723 to update the active color and remove the not used `selected` variable. Hover is trickier—curious about how you pulled it off as we don't have some akin to `is_marked`.

Hey @danilo-leal, sorry for making that much noise. I love your design for the diagnostics and having the diagnostics in the project panel makes my DX so, so much better, but can we try to address this issue before https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/18182 makes it into the normal release? I proposed a solution in https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/20760, can you take a look at that please?

review_comments: The idea is to keep a state for all the events and not do dynamic style adjustments with `.hover(|style| ...`, so we can pass the same color to the background and to the knockout icons. I think this logic replicates exactly the previous behaviour.
Do the listener callbacks run potentially on a different thread and this HashSet should be threadsafe?
Yeah, listeners run on foreground IIRC, so we should be good here. Besides, it wouldn't compile if it wasn't thread-safe 😄

This was a tricky one. We had a `.hover` style adjustment in the div that contains the ListItem AND ListItem sets the background color as well if the ListItem is selectable. `selectable` does not change the behaviour of click events or anything else, it only controls the coloring.
